P1.evidence: No setter pre-qualification exists to read back. No four-part frame and no frame agreement — the rep went straight from small talk to the open question: "So, look, man, brief me in. What brought you here, actually? I think we can start it from here."

P2.evidence: Injuries were run properly — "Do you have any injuries or anything that limits your movements?" followed by real probing that surfaced months of being unable to do dips. Training week, results and diet were all asked directly: "How long have you been going into those calisthenics classes?", "Did you see any improvements in terms of your body composition?", "You mentioned nutrition... How does it look like right now? And be honest." Against that: age, height and weight were never asked — height and weight only surfaced because the prospect volunteered them while describing his stomach. Health conditions were never asked at all. Sleep was the prospect's own diagnosis and the rep followed it ("Is it because of work obligations too?") without ever asking quantity or quality directly. Energy through the day was never touched.

P3.evidence: The goal was asked and named — "Is that the goal for you?" / "The goal is for me to lose this belly fat" — and the bridge ran almost verbatim: "what's the biggest reason that you actually want to do this? Why? What's your why?" But the answer that came back was still surface ("mostly health-wise... it also doesn't look good") and the rep did not drive deeper. The family thread was opened and abandoned inside four turns: "do you have kids?" / "No, no, no. I'm single" / "Are you planning on having one?" / "Yeah, I hope so" / "Inshallah. All right." This is the notable failure of the call — the prospect had already handed over a full identity crisis about the family business, his father and wanting to leave city life, and none of it was ever connected to the training decision or reflected back.

P4.evidence: Root cause landed well. "Looking at everything what you've tried, why do you think, what keeps happening that you cannot hit this goal?" got "there's no discipline whatsoever", and "why do you think, where this lack of discipline is coming from?" drove it to sleep as the anchor. The prospect then named the structural gap himself — "I can easily commit if I have a proper plan, or a proper pathway that I can follow" — and the rep reflected it back cleanly: "So it's about having a structure, a clear path, and a guidance from someone who will take you by the hand." What was missing: the past-attempts inventory was assumed rather than asked (the meal-prep history was volunteered), and the "information isn't the problem" line was never run even though the prospect served it up on a plate — "I'm aware of all of the nutritional values, and I'm aware of what's good and what's not, I'm just not committed to it."

P5.evidence: The consequence frame did not run in any form. No two-year question, no settling question, no why-not, no line in the sand. The closest thing in the whole call is a throwaway: "you have two options, whether get fatter, better, or lose the belly." This is a 20-weight phase skipped entirely, and it is the direct reason the $6,000 had nothing behind it when it landed.

P6.evidence: The all-in question ran twice and got a clean answer: "are you willing to actually show up and do the work? Because, like, totally honest, it's going to be hard", and then "If we can figure out all the details and, and, and scheduling, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work?" / "A hundred percent." The belief question about structure and the right person in his corner was only approximated ("How do you feel in general about the structure and about the program?", "Does it check your boxes?"). The ordering is wrong: the script wants the verbal yes before presenting anything, and the rep delivered all three pillars from 00:24 to 00:34 and only then ran the commitment check at 00:34:35.

P11.evidence: The call never reached payment. The rep pre-announced the sequence — "I'll walk you through the investment, get you on board with Trevor's. Schedule on a call with him" — but the price was met with a budget objection and the call was ended by the prospect twenty seconds into the finance conversation. No payment, no Trevor call booked, no agreement, no Skool link.

objection_plays.detail: Materially better than the same rep's other call on this date, and visibly the product of his 1-1 that morning. Isolation ran: "So, apart from the finances, everything is good?" The budget was surfaced: "what were you thinking about the budget?" → "$2,000, 2,500". The upfront norm ran: "most of the clients that are working with us just take the investment upfront, you know, just put it on a credit card." The custom-plan framing ran almost word for word as coached: "we don't have payment plans. We can do them, but it's super custom." And the permission question ran: "would you be comfortable to have an open conversation about the finances and how we can actually make that work for you?" What did not run: the "you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place" reframe, and every one of the six financial-picture questions — cash on hand, monthly surplus, number of cards, available credit, used versus available, investments. The prospect answered the permission question by pivoting to a written-offer request, the rep followed him there, and the play never resumed before the call ended.

Script gap. Two distinct unscripted objections landed together and neither has a play. First, a functioning cheaper alternative: he has been coached in calisthenics for over a year with visible results, and intends to meet two in-person trainers in Jordan and compare programmes and pricing. Second, a request for written terms to enable that comparison — "I still would need something concrete written, so I can make a fair comparison." The rep's answer was that nothing written exists because everything is custom, which left the comparison to happen entirely outside the conversation with no artefact carrying his side of it. He did begin the right question — "what's the most important... that you're going to be looking for, apart from the price?" — but was interrupted before an answer.

"Let's get back to this conversation next week" at 00:39:57. None of the play ran — no "do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal", no "thinking isn't the problem, deciding is". Mitigating context: the deferral was forced by an external interruption at the prospect's end ("We go in five minutes"), not by resistance, and the rep did secure a dated, confirmed follow-up rather than a vague one.

notes: Best discovery in the batch paired with a completely absent consequence frame — he built a detailed picture, got a genuine 100% commitment, and then presented price with no cost of inaction established, which is why a well-qualified prospect went straight to comparison shopping. Two specific coaching points: drive the why past "it doesn't look good" into the family-business and identity material the prospect volunteered unprompted, and run P5 before the number. Credit where due — the open-wallet isolation and permission framing from his 1-1 that morning transferred to a live call the same day.
